newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Achinsky alumina plant in receivership.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Achinsky alumina plant in receivership.

text.p: Russia's Achinsky Alumina Plant will be put under the administration of trade group Alfa-Eko for 18 months but will not be liquidated, a regional court ruled on Wednesday.

Alexander Kryukov, head of the Krasnoyarsk territorial bankruptcy agency, which has jurisdiction over Achinsky Glinozyomny Kombinat, said in a telephone interview that the regional arbitration court had decided to halt bankruptcy proceedings at Achinsky.
He said the court had appointed an Alfa-Eko representative to manage Achinsky after meeting the plant's creditors.

"Alfa-Eko is prepared to support our enterprise," Kryukov said, adding that the plant needed 77 billion roubles in investment and that under the court ruling, Alfa-Eko had until March 15, 1997 to present a rescue plan for the plant.
Alfa-Eko, one of Russia's largest oil and soft commodities traders, declined to comment.
Kryukov said Achinsky owed 1.1 trillion roubles and was owed 320 billion as of December. Government officials had targeted the plant in October, saying it could face liquidation over unpaid taxes.
The Krasnoyarsk aluminium smelter, one of Russia's largest, holds a 24.5 percent stake in Achinsky.
An industry source said Achinsky accounts for about one quarter of Russia's output of alumina, the raw material used to make aluminium, but he declined to give the plant's capacity.
Achinsk is part of a planned financial-industrial group that includes Krasnoyarsk and Ukraine's Mikolayiv alumina producer.
Alfa-Eko is affiliated with Alfa Bank, one of Russia's biggest.
